answer: Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ripple of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The pearl is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the quill. The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, published publicly on failure, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name.
